introduction.text: The Chiesa di Santa Maria dei Miracoli is a Baroque church in Rome’s Campo Marzio district, notable for its miraculous origin, its twin relationship with Santa Maria in Montesanto, and its architectural and artistic features.

history.description: A miracle on 20 June 1325 led to the construction of a small chapel dedicated to the Virgin, the origin of the church.
In 1525 Pope Clement VII entrusted the chapel to the nearby Hospital of San Giacomo degli Incurabili.
The chapel passed to the Capuchins in 1529, but was flooded by the Tiber the following year.
In 1590 the image of the Madonna was moved to the newly built church of San Giacomo in Augusta.
Pope Alessandro VII ordered a new church on Piazza del Popolo in 1661 to house the image.
Construction of the new church began in 1675.
The church was completed in 1679 and consecrated two years later.
In 1793 the church was granted to the Confraternity of the Most Holy Sacrament.
In 1856 it passed to the Arciconfraternita of San Gregorio Taumaturgo.
Since 1915 the church has been administered by the Priests of the Sacred Heart of Jesus of Bétharram.

design.description: The façade features a deep rectangular pronao crowned by a tympanum bearing the name of benefactor Cardinal Gastaldi.
A cupola octagonally shaped and covered with slate tiles was designed and built by Carlo Fontana.
The bell tower, mirroring that of Santa Maria in Montesanto, was attributed to Francesco Navone.
The interior follows a circular plan with four side chapels and a deep presbytery, designed by Carlo Rainaldi and executed by Carlo Fontana.

art.description: Ten statues of saints on the exterior balustrade were executed between 1676 and 1677 by Filippo Carcani, Ercole Ferrata, and others.
The central altar features a 1646 copy of the Madonna dei Miracoli, originally a 16th‑century fresco.
Interior decorations include stucco work by Antonio Raggi and a marble bust of Pope Pio VI.
